cards.a: The distance from the centre of one framing member to the centre of the next, e.g. studs at 16 in (406 mm) o.c.
cards.tip: Centre to centre, not edge to edge.

cards.a: A full-height stud beside a wall opening, running sole plate to top plate, that the jack stud fastens to.
A shortened stud that supports the header ends and carries the load down to the sole plate.
A short stud above a header or below a sill that keeps regular spacing for sheathing and finishes.
The horizontal bottom member of a framed wall; also called the bottom plate.
cards.tip: The wall stands on its sole.

cards.a: The horizontal member at the top of a framed wall, usually doubled to tie walls together.
Lumber volume equal to 1 in × 12 in × 1 ft. BF = (T″ × W″ × L′) ÷ 12.
cards.tip: Thickness and width in inches, length in feet.

cards.a: The natural bow along a board's edge; framing members install crown up so loads straighten them.
